chapter_theme: Pambatti's sermon continues through three sections. Against desire for women (2030 to 2038) he lists the lover's similes, breasts as Meru, eyes as swords, hair as cloud, saliva as nectar, bird-names and sweet-names, and sets against each the body's filth, saying we have scolded, renounced and thrown it off. On the body's nature (2039 to 2048) he reads it as a potter's vessel of filth and blood not worth a dry stick, a ten-month kiln not worth half a coin, a pot that breaks for dogs and vultures, a water bubble, a stinking fish that washing cannot clean, a nine-holed bellows, a wooden puppet on the string of life, and a ship of ten nadis, ten airs and seven dhatus. Against inner attachment (2049 to 2054) he gives the images of the lotus leaf, the tamarind in its shell, oil and water, and the insect leaving the mud, and tells the hearer to open the eye of knowledge and see the open space and the form of consciousness.
structure_note: Three printed sections: பெண்ணாசை விலக்கல் (2030 to 2038), சரீரத்தின் குணம் (2039 to 2048) and அகப்பற்று நீக்கல் (2049 to 2054, continued in chapter 105). The stanzas against women fall into two kinds: 2031 to 2034 and 2038 answer a flattering simile with the body's reality; 2035 to 2037 are bare lists of endearments followed by the refusal to utter them. The body stanzas each carry one image. The refrain is ஆடாய் பாம்பே throughout.

2030.reading: The peacock-woman with globed breasts and bee-like eyes we spat on and scolded, swallowing her with the mind as if she were milk; and we killed and ate the Death-kite that rides the thick-bodied buffalo; dance.
2030.nuance: சித்தப்பால் விழுங்கி is obscure; it may say the woman was consumed by the mind (as a figure of seeing through her), or that the Siddhar drank the milk of the mind, or read சித்தப் பால், the side of the mind. The buffalo-rider is Yama, and the kite (பருந்து) his bird; the stanza boasts of conquering both desire and death, in the Siddhar's first person plural.

2031.reading: They call a skin that will shrivel away a round breast and liken it to great Meru; be sure that those who have fallen into the stinking well of the womb will be ruined, and dance.
2031.nuance: The stanza sets the poets' simile (மகமேரு) against the physician's fact (வற்றும் தோல், skin that will shrivel). யோனிக் கேணி, the well of the womb, is the Siddhars' usual image for the pit of desire and birth.

2032.reading: Those without strength of mind describe an eye that oozes filth as the equal of a sharp sword; the owl-men who talk of its fine quality become food for the belly of the pit; dance.
2032.nuance: குருநலம் is read as குரு (the eye's beauty or lustre) rather than the guru; கும்பி, the pit, is a hell in Siddhar and Saiva usage, so the owl-men (கூகை, blind by day) feed hell. The reading of கும்பிக்கே இரை as hell's food rather than the belly's is traditional and not certain.

2033.reading: They call tangled stinking hair a rich cloud and say the breasts are like golden cups; melting and melting, they think of the woman in their heart and do not think of the Stainless One; dance.
2033.nuance: நெக்கு நெக்கு உருகி, melting and melting, is the devotee's vocabulary of bhakti, here given to the lover; the stanza's charge is a misdirected melting, for the woman instead of the நிமலன்.

2034.reading: The owl-men without sense call reeking spittle good nectar and a nose full of mucus a fine bud; they do not know the state of the King; dance.
2034.nuance: எச்சில், saliva, is ritually polluting in Tamil usage, and the stanza turns the lover's kiss into a breach of purity. கோனிலை, the King's state, is the state of the Lord that the lovers miss.

2035.reading: Peacock, cuckoo, ruby, deer, honey, heavenly nectar, the one who matches the graceful swan and peacock: we have stopped saying these and driven them off; dance.
2035.nuance: The first of three stanzas that are only lists of endearments; the content is the refusal to speak them (ஓதாமற் கடிந்து). The Siddhar's renunciation is of a vocabulary.

2036.reading: Lightning-creeper, bright lamp, slender one, vine, Menaka, cane-sugar lump, sugar-candy: we have scolded these away without uttering them; dance.
2036.nuance: Menaka is the celestial courtesan who seduced Vishvamitra; the list moves from light to sweetness and ends with the Siddhar's refusal, as in 2035.

2037.reading: Lady, doll, gold, flower-Lakshmi, my treasure, koel-fruit, garlanded one, cuckoo: we have renounced them without saying them; dance.
2037.nuance: என்றன் பொக்கிஷம், my treasure, is the one word of possession in the three lists; the stanza's துறந்தோம் (we renounced) treats the words themselves as the possession given up.

2038.reading: Knowing it for ourselves as turmeric smeared on a pot of filth, as a coloured skin over a swarming nest of worms, as stinking mud in a pit of water, we threw it away; dance.
2038.nuance: The three images answer the three kinds of flattery: the painted surface, the skin, the wet hollow. தான் அறிந்து, knowing it oneself, is the ground of the renunciation; the Siddhar does not cite a text.

2039.reading: Taking clay from a pit of filth and mixing the lump in a stream of blood, the vessel the clever potter makes is not worth even a dry stick; dance.
2039.nuance: The potter is the Lord or the father, the clay and blood the seed and the womb's blood; வறகோட்டுக்கும் ஆகாது, not worth a dry twig, is the body's price. The image is the Siddhars' and Tirumular's pot, with the making added.

2040.reading: Two people gathered the clay and one shaped it; the kiln set for ten months, however precious it is, that kiln is not worth half a coin; dance.
2040.nuance: The riddle continues 2039: the two are the parents, the one who shapes is the Lord or the embryo's own karma, the ten-month kiln the womb. சூளை (kiln) is also read as the body baked in it; either way the valuation is the point.

2041.reading: The snake that bit as if in jest: it swelled greatly for many to see, and when a woman physician looked at it, it came away together with the bag; dance.
2041.nuance: The stanza is a riddle and the sense turns on the cipher. One reading: desire bit like a joke, the body swelled in pregnancy or pride before all, and when the woman (death, or Shakti, or the vaalai) looked, life left with the bag of the body. Another: a plain anecdote of a snakebite misdiagnosed, ending in death. பரியாரம் is read as பரிகாரி, physician. The reading above keeps the stanza's images and does not fix the cipher.

2042.reading: If the pot that holds the foul stench of pus and excrement, thick blood and fat should break, dog and jackal, the great ghoul and the vulture will eat it saying it is theirs; dance.
2042.nuance: நமதென்றே தின்னும், eat it as their own, is the stanza's edge: the body that was 'mine' becomes theirs. The list of eaters is the burning-ground company of the Naladiyar and Pattinathar.

2043.reading: Like a bubble that rises on water and loses its standing, the body will not stay but will surely depart; so seize and keep following the one who created the many lives on earth, and dance.
2043.nuance: நிச்சயம் என்றே, as a certainty, is the stanza's weight; the bubble is the common image, and the instruction is to hold the Creator instead of the body.

2044.reading: If you wash a stinking fish many times in good water every day, will its stench go? So the body you speak of, by bathing in many rivers, will not lose the impurity it holds; dance.
2044.nuance: The stanza is an argument against holy bathing: the fish's stench is in the fish, and the body's மலம் is in the body. மலம் is both the bodily filth of the section and the Saiva impurity that binds the soul, and the stanza lets the two senses meet.

2045.reading: The fruiting tree takes many blows from stones; the body that carries the fruit of its deeds takes its rebukes; say that those who have gained a fitting austerity are the ones who live, and worship the holy feet, and dance.
2045.nuance: The tree stoned for its fruit and the body struck for its karma make a proverb-like pair; கண்டனை is read as rebuke or chastisement, and வத்து (for வஸ்து, the Real) in the last line is a guess at a garbled word. The stanza's claim is that tapas, not the body, is what lives.

2046.reading: A torn bellows with nine mouths that cannot be described: because a great wind entered it, speech arose; for those who do not know the Lord's state, this bellows is food for the burning earth; dance.
2046.nuance: நவவாயில், nine gates, is the standard count of the body's openings; துருத்தி, the smith's bellows, is the Siddhars' image for a body that lives only by the wind in it. Speech itself (பேச்சு) is reduced to the wind's effect.

2047.reading: Making a figure of earth like a wooden puppet and fitting to it the string called the fat living soul, the moment the one who moved it from behind the screen has finished, the body falls; know this clearly and dance.
2047.nuance: The puppet has three parts: the earthen figure, the string that is the jivan, and the hidden mover behind the curtain (திரைக்குள் இருந்து அசைப்போன்). The body falls not when the string breaks but when the mover stops, which places the cause of death in the Lord's will.

2048.reading: The wooden ship joined of ten nadis, ten airs and seven dhatus will lurch and fall; resolve to sail the fitting ship on the one flood for ever, and dance.
2048.nuance: The body is counted as the ten channels, ten vital airs and seven bodily constituents of the medical texts, and called a ship that will capsize. இசைவான கப்பல், the agreeable ship, that sails on the ஏக வெள்ளம் (one flood) is not identified; tradition takes it as the breath or the soul carried on the flood of grace or of the Supreme.

2049.reading: As water does not stay on the lotus leaf, push away desire for the world everywhere, and worship and worship and worship the feet of the Light that shines as a pure gem; dance.
2049.nuance: The lotus leaf is the Gita's and Sivavakkiyar's image for living in the world untouched by it; the stanza pairs it with a triple தொழுது, so detachment and worship are the same act.

2050.reading: Cutting the bonds of everything that has been forbidden, deceit, killing, lust and the rest, open the eye of knowledge, examine and see the clear open space and the form of consciousness, and with a clarified mind dance.
2050.nuance: The stanza puts ethics first (கள்ளம் கொலை காமம், the forbidden deeds) and vision second: ஞானக் கண், the eye of knowledge, sees the வெட்டவெளி, the open space, and the சிற்சொரூபம், the form of pure consciousness. The two names for what is seen, space and consciousness, are given as one.

2051.reading: Like the tamarind fruit with its shell, stay among kin without ties to them; stand, mind, in the supreme stainless one, and dance knowing that your companion there is the bare void.
2051.nuance: The ripe tamarind lies loose inside its shell: present but unattached. நின் துணைதான் வெறும் பாழ், your only companion is the empty void, can be read as consolation (the void is the companion) or as warning (you will have no companion but emptiness); the Siddhar sense of பாழ் as the Real favours the first.

2052.reading: Like the insect that moves in the mud and then leaves the mud, after seeing the doings of those who live in step with the country, one must take and walk the path that reaches the supreme space that is spoken of; dance.
2052.nuance: திரிபிள்ளைப்பூச்சி is read as the mud-wasp or larva that lives in mud and flies free of it; the identification is not sure. தேசத்தோடு ஒத்து வாழ்வார், those who live conformed to the land, are the worldly, and the stanza asks the hearer to watch them and then leave as the insect leaves the mud.

2053.reading: As oil and water have no bond between them, so one must always be on this earth; see the light that is the eye of the eye, cut your bonds and live, and dance.
2053.nuance: கண்ணுக்குக் கண்ணான ஒளி, the light that is eye to the eye, is the Upanishadic figure of the awareness behind seeing; the oil-and-water simile makes detachment a difference of nature, not of effort.

2054.reading: As vomited rice and curry and roots are a clean sight to the eyes, scold the world you are caught in with a 'faugh', and be clear so as to see the fine feet, and dance.
2054.nuance: The simile is strained: கக்கிவிட்ட சோறு, vomited food, a clean sight, is read ironically (what was eaten returns as what no one wants) or as the way the vomiter sees it, with disgust and finality; the stanza wants the world seen with the same finished disgust (சீயென்று ஒறுத்து).

links.note: The Naladiyar's fool calls a pot that seeps filth from nine openings 'broad-shouldered one' because its dark skin dazzles him; Pambatti's lovers call a skin that will shrivel a round breast like Meru and fall into the stinking well. Both oppose the flattering name to the anatomy, and both blame the eye that is dazzled.

Pattinathar says karma took the form of a woman, rounded into the breasts men speak of, and pushed him into the pit of filth and blood; Pambatti says the breasts are shrivelling skin called Meru and the womb a stinking well that ruins those who fall in. Pattinathar confesses the fall; Pambatti warns against it.

The Naladiyar refuses the men who call eyes water-lilies, carp or spears, having seen the eye as a scooped-out palm fruit; Pambatti says those without strength of mind call an eye that oozes filth a sword. The same simile (the eye as a blade) is rejected by the same means, a look at the organ.

The Naladiyar's untaught men call smiles jasmine buds and pearls, and the poet answers with the teeth and bones scattered in the burning ground; Pambatti's owl-men call spittle nectar and a mucous nose a bud. Both reduce the praised mouth to its fluids and remains.

Tirumular's potter shapes pots from the tank's clay, and when the body breaks no one keeps it even a moment; Pambatti's potter takes clay from the pit of filth and mixes it with blood, and the vessel is not worth a dry stick. Tirumular's image is of the body's end, Pambatti's of its making; the valuation is the same.

Sivavakkiyar asks when he will become the Lord's subject before this salted pot breaks and takes a womb again; Pambatti describes how the pot was made, from filth-pit clay and blood by the potter. Both use the pot for the body and both set the Lord against its breaking.

The Naladiyar asks whether those who praise sandal and garlands have not seen vultures tear at the stinking cart once its axle breaks; Pambatti's pot of pus, blood and fat breaks and dog, jackal, ghoul and vulture eat it as their own. The broken vehicle and its scavengers are the same lesson against praising the body.

The Naladiyar's firm-minded see the body as a bubble in pelting rain and resolve to end their wandering; Pambatti's body is a bubble rising on water that will surely depart, and the hearer is to hold the Creator. The image is the same; the Naladiyar draws renunciation from it and Pambatti devotion.

Tirumular says those who know only bathing cannot join the Lord, who is within the mind; Pambatti says bathing in many rivers no more removes the body's impurity than washing removes a fish's stench. Both deny that holy water purifies; Tirumular offers the inner holy waters instead, Pambatti the knowledge of the Lord's state.

The Kural says outer purity comes through water and inner purity is seen through truth; Pambatti says the body's impurity does not leave by bathing in rivers. Pambatti goes further than the Kural, denying even the outer cleansing, since the stench is in the fish; but both locate real purity elsewhere than in water.

Sivavakkiyar asks when he will throw off this bellows that the wind blows and reach the Lord; Pambatti's body is a torn nine-mouthed bellows in which the great wind produced speech, food for the burning earth for those who do not know the Lord. Both use the smith's bellows for a body animated only by breath.

Tirumular counts eight that go out and eighteen that come in through the nine gates, with the snake and the horses of the breath; Pambatti's bellows has nine mouths and lives by the wind that entered it. Both count the body by its nine openings and its breath, Tirumular as a yogic puzzle and Pambatti as a memento mori.

Pattinathar tells his heart to hold the wretched body as a puppet show and life as water from an overturned pot; Pambatti's body is a clay puppet on the string of the soul, falling the moment the mover behind the screen stops. Pattinathar names the show, Pambatti names the puppeteer.

Tirumular says Hara makes the elements he spread dance like the deed that makes a false puppet dance, and so settles the soul in awareness; Pambatti's hidden mover behind the screen works the string of the soul, and the body falls when he stops. Both put the puppeteer behind life and death; Tirumular calls it grace, Pambatti only says the body falls.

Sivavakkiyar asks when he will put kin away like the lotus leaf spreading on the water; Pambatti tells the snake to push away desire for the world as water does not stay on the lotus leaf, and worship the Light's feet. The same leaf, as a question in one poet and an instruction in the other.

Sivavakkiyar asks when he will become like the ripe tamarind, firm within its shell yet apart from it, though he lives with troublesome women; Pambatti says to stay among kin like the tamarind fruit in its shell, without ties, and to stand in the stainless Supreme. Both apply the image to living among one's own without attachment.

source_issues: 2035 line 4 ஓதாமற் கடிந்துவிட் றாடாய் is defective; a syllable (டோ or டே) is missing before the refrain (compare 2036 கடிந்தோமென் றாடாய்).
2045 line 4 வத்துத்திரு வடிதொழு தாடாய் is garbled; வத்து is read as வஸ்து (the Real) but may be a corruption of another word.
2030 line 2 சித்தப்பால் விழுங்கியே is obscure and may be corrupt.
2052 line 1 திரிபிள்ளைப்பூச்சி is an unidentified insect name; the simile is read from the context of leaving the mud.
